brief.title: Reliable weekly reports for a volunteer club
brief.audience: Python learners who can define a function and iterate a list but have not built a complete tool
brief.outcome: Independently build and test a reproducible weekly activity report, diagnose incorrect totals, and explain input and presentation decisions
brief.deliverable: A local standard-library Python reporting tool with fixtures, tests, clear output and a handover README
brief.constraints: Python 3.12 standard library only; name/minutes records; no accounts; small deterministic fixtures; use exact skill strings consistently
brief.exclusions: Web frameworks, databases, machine learning, deployment, external packages and actual personal data

reviewChecks: Repeated and empty records have explicit expected results
Input and presentation contracts agree across lessons
Tests reject overwriting instead of accumulating totals
Learners write meaningful checks without exposing private QA artifacts
The final tool is usable by a volunteer organizer

brief.title: A reliable reading queue in JavaScript
brief.audience: Learners who know JavaScript functions and arrays but have not tested a complete local application
brief.outcome: Build and test a deterministic reading queue that preserves item identity, handles duplicate titles and explains its input decisions
brief.deliverable: A dependency-free Node.js command-line reading queue with JSON fixtures, node:test checks and a handover guide
brief.constraints: Node.js 24; built-in modules only; synthetic book titles; no network; deterministic IDs supplied by fixtures; use exact skill strings consistently
brief.exclusions: Browser UI, frameworks, package installation, databases, scraping and paid services

reviewChecks: Malformed persisted input is explained and handled
No hidden clock, random or network dependency enters tests
Public interfaces remain compatible between milestones
Transfer changes one real requirement instead of repeating the guided example

brief.title: From a club survey to a defensible recommendation
brief.audience: Learners comfortable reading tables and calculating percentages who have not designed an analysis
brief.outcome: Produce an accessible, reproducible analysis of a synthetic club survey and defend a bounded recommendation without causal overclaims
brief.deliverable: A documented Python standard-library survey analysis with fixtures, clear tables, missing-value decisions and a recommendation memo
brief.constraints: Python 3.12 standard library only; original synthetic non-sensitive survey; deterministic calculations; every numerical example includes checkable expected results
brief.exclusions: Personal data, inferential significance claims, causal claims, machine learning, external packages and web scraping

reviewChecks: Denominators and missing-value decisions are explicit
Every numerical worked example is internally consistent
No sample statistic is presented as a causal conclusion
Written recommendations state limitations and plausible alternatives
